name: screenshots
//: The curated fixture, the vendored renderer font and the durable note behind the README's captures are a project like everything else, so a change to one is selected by the graph rather than escaping it. Its layer is documentation: nothing here is reachable from a crate, it depends on no other project, and the only edge is the one `workspace` has to every project. Its two checks are STATIC — neither takes a screenshot, and no target here captures, which is what keeps the capture out of `just check`, `just gate` and CI's check job exactly as .github/workflows/visual-docs.yml and screenshots/AGENTS.md say. The capture itself is `just screenshots`, which is not an Nx target at all, and .githooks/pre-push runs it after the gate only when what is being pushed can change a rendered shot. llmlint: ignore-file[expensive_tests_stay_behind_their_own_edge] JSON has no comment to scope this to the `lint` target's workspaceRoot inputs, which is what it is about: that check reconciles the README, the workflow and the committed images, so it has to re-run when one of them moves — and Nx selects a PROJECT rather than a target, so those inputs select `test` too. There is no expensive tier behind that edge to move: both checks clone with `git clone --shared` and the whole target finishes in under two seconds (measured). Dropping the inputs instead would stop the reconciliation re-running when a README image is deleted, which is the defect it exists to catch.

bootstrap.//: Nothing to provision, deliberately: the pinned renderer is installed on demand by `just screenshots-tools`, and putting a screenshot tool on the gate's provisioning path would make an informational tier a prerequisite of the gate.

format.//: Uncached: it rewrites the tree in place. Only this project's own JSON is formatted — biome has no formatter for Markdown front matter, a TrueType font or an SVG.

lint.//: The static half, and a lint rather than a test because it reads files and reconciles them: every version this capture pins and restates, the scene inventory against the committed baseline, and every image the README embeds against what is committed. It takes no screenshot and needs neither screencomp nor the renderer, so it runs in CI's check job like every other lint. The workspaceRoot inputs are what SELECTS this project as well as what hashes it — a README that drops an image, or a workflow whose two screencomp pins part, has to re-run this.

typecheck.//: Declared and empty. Target names are uniform because `nx affected` fans out by name, and there is nothing here between reading a file and running it: the capture machinery is shell, whose static analysis is the bash 3.2 scan under `scripts:lint`, and the fixture is data the real binary parses in the `test` target's own scenes.

test.//: The first drives the REAL pre-push guard and the real hook through every outcome each owes, with screencomp and the capture stubbed at the subprocess seam the way scripts/check-pre-push-provisioning.sh stubs `just` — so a guard that stopped blocking on drift, or started capturing on a push that cannot change a shot, fails here rather than when the workflow disagrees with a merged commit. The second drives the renderer resolver and the baseline writer against a stand-in tool location and a stand-in installer, as scripts/check-scoped-release-plz.sh does for the other scoped tool: no network, and nothing installed on the host is read or touched. Uncached for the reason the workspace project's own test target is: both clone this repository into a scratch tree, which no input glob in this tree describes. Serial because each clones one.

coverage.//: Declared and empty. The 95% line floor is measured by instrumenting a compiled crate or an interpreted SDK; there is no line coverage for a shell script or a Markdown fixture, and what stands in its place is the guard check above driving the real guard until it refuses.
